Senses.Explanation: To abandon the root and chase the branches is to substitute sought objects, inherited words, or ornamental learning for the root named in each case. Mazu, Dahui, and Zhenjing use the same critical contrast against different substitutions. The root-and-branches idiom becomes a Chan verdict on replacing direct responsibility with scriptures, phrases, learning, or a sought awakening. Mazu, Dahui, and Zhenjing identify different discarded roots, so the entry describes the shared critical relation without declaring one universal meaning for the root. Different proposed roots and branches instantiate one abandonment-and-pursuit relation, not separate senses.
